F21 Relationship to host platform

Host platform

F21.host-platform The platform this surface runs on.

● supported

Value: Codex local surfaces are the ChatGPT desktop app, the IDE extension and the CLI, which run on users' computers; this does not include using Codex in the cloud. The desktop app, CLI, IDE extension and SDK read the same local configuration layers (model_provider is set in ~/.codex/config.toml).

F01 Loop and built-in tools

Loop shape

F01.loop-shape How a turn runs: plan, tool call, result, stop.

● supported

Value: A turn is one exchange, usually a user prompt plus the agent's response and actions. `turn/start` adds user input to a thread and begins Codex generation, streaming events. In the tool loop, Codex receives a call, executes the tool, and submits its result. In Codex cloud chats the agent runs terminal commands in a loop, editing code and running checks.

Turn and step limits

F01.turn-limits Caps on turns, steps or tokens per run, and stop conditions.

● supported

Value: Auto-review interrupts the turn after 3 consecutive denials (open-source implementation), or 10 denials within a rolling window of the last 50. Shell execution tool

F01.shell-tool How commands run: shell, working directory, timeouts, output handling.

● supported

Value: Shell-based tools can use login-shell semantics (default true; when false, `login = true` requests are rejected and omitted `login` defaults to non-login shells). Max empty `write_stdin` poll window is set by `background_terminal_max_timeout` (ms; default 5m). User-initiated `thread/shellCommand` runs outside the sandbox with full access.

Web search and fetch tools

F01.web-tools Built-in web search or page fetch, and their controls.

◐ partial

Value: Codex enables web search by default for local chats and serves results from a web search cache, an OpenAI-maintained index of pre-indexed results rather than live pages. Mode is one of disabled | cached | indexed | live (default cached); `--search` switches to live browsing.

Limitation: Hosted web search isn't available on Bedrock Runtime.

  • E-codex-cli-00463

    Codex enables web search by default for local chats and serves results from a web search cache. This reduces exposure to prompt injection from arbitrary live content.

Automatic compaction

Persistent memory

F02.persistent-memory Memory that survives sessions: files, notes or an auto-memory store.

● supported

Value: Memories let ChatGPT and Codex carry useful context from earlier work into future work. Memory scope and loading

F02.memory-scope-loading Where memory lives, who sees it, and when it is loaded.

● supported

Value: The main memory files live under `~/.codex/memories/`. ChatGPT web uses ChatGPT memory; local Codex clients use a separate local store, and the IDE extension uses the connected Codex host's local memory store. A setting (default true) lets Codex skip injecting existing memories into future sessions.

F03 Instruction files

Auto-loaded files

F03.auto-loaded-files File names loaded without being asked (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, rules).

● supported

Value: Codex reads `AGENTS.md` files before doing any work, discovering them by walking up from the working directory until it reaches a project root. An ignored `AGENTS.override.md` is copied into local managed worktrees automatically. Starting or resuming a thread returns `instructionSources`, an array of loaded instruction-file paths.

Precedence and scoping

F03.precedence-scoping Which file wins and how directories nest.

● supported

Value: Codex can load a global file from your Codex home directory plus repo-specific files; files closer to the working directory take precedence. Per-tool rules

F04.per-tool-rules Allow, ask or deny a named tool.

● supported

Value: Individual MCP tools can use approval_mode = "prompt"; prompt rules can cover each sensitive command. Destructive app/MCP tool calls always require approval when the tool advertises a destructive annotation (unless it advertises a read annotation, which takes priority). Rules allow, prompt for, or deny command prefixes or permission exceptions.
